prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1070; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact. Statements from two independent witnesses and the other driver match the account given at first notice, and scene photographs are consistent with the reported sequence of events.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage to the rear bumper, trunk, and tail lamp assembly is largely in line with the described impact speed and direction. No prior damage to the vehicle is recorded or reported, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy effective period. The driver is confirmed as a named driver on the policy.

Entry 4: Medical records received from the claimant's treating provider. The reported shoulder injury fits well with the kind and force of this crash. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from prior records or the claimant's history.

Entry 5: Counsel's office provided treatment summary. Care followed a typical course of physical therapy and follow-up visits, tapering as the claimant improved. The claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation with the adjuster to date.

Entry 6: Reviewed the file for the current stage of the claim. Liability and injury information are consistent across all sources, and the file is ready for evaluation of the bodily injury and property damage components.
